summary: Steel 30-ft lookout above Rimforest, built 1933 after a wooden tower at Grass Valley collapsed; a Mountains Foundation history gives conflicting 1922 and 1934 dates.

access.note: Open to the public for the 2025 season per the Mountains Foundation. The Forest Service page showed a temporary-closure notice and a winter closure when it was read.

visit.trail_note: Two miles up a paved road from Bear Springs Road, off Highway 18 near Rim Forest.

events.note: Steel 30-ft tower. Newspapers date construction to May 1933 and say it replaced a wooden tower at Grass Valley that collapsed under snow.
Registered on the National Historic Lookout Register January 6, 1999
Opened all year because of high fire danger

corrections.current: 1934 replaced: the old tower, damaged by lightning and heavy snow, was replaced by the present 30-ft tower
corrections.proposed: 1933 built: steel 30-ft tower begun in May 1933; the wooden tower it replaced at Grass Valley collapsed under snow in January 1933
corrections.why: The 1933 newspaper reports date construction to May 1933 and place the collapsed wooden tower at Grass Valley, not on this peak. The 1934 replacement date comes from the Mountains Foundation page, which the newspapers contradict.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register and the 1933 newspapers agree on 1933 for the steel tower. The Mountains Foundation gives 1922 for an earlier tower on this peak and 1934 for the present one. The newspapers place the earlier wooden tower at Grass Valley, so this is only partly resolved.

notes_for_editor: The first-tower dispute is the main issue. The Mountains Foundation (1922 80-ft tower on the peak; 1934 damage and replacement) conflicts with the 1933 newspaper transcriptions (80-ft wooden tower at Grass Valley collapsed January 1933; steel tower on Strawberry Peak begun May 1933) and with the register's 1933. The newspaper text comes from a transcription page quoting The San Bernardino County Sun; I did not check it against the original paper. The corrections proposal depends on that. Access is set to public because the Mountains Foundation says it was open for the 2025 season, but the Forest Service copy showed a temporary-closure notice and a winter closure, so re-check current status before publishing. The staffing as_of date is undated because the register page is undated.
